title: Quiet Firing: 3 Signs Your Boss Wants You Out
hook: Quiet firing: 3 signs you're being pushed out.

scenes.caption: If your boss does these three things in your weekly meetings, you are not being overlooked — you are being quietly managed out.
scenes.caption_roman: If your boss does these three things in your weekly meetings, you are not being overlooked — you are being quietly managed out.

scenes.caption: Sign one: information starvation. Key emails, client updates, and meeting invites suddenly stop arriving in your inbox.
scenes.caption_roman: Sign one: information starvation. Key emails, client updates, and meeting invites suddenly stop arriving in your inbox.

scenes.caption: Sign two: moving goalposts. Projects you delivered perfectly are suddenly critiqued with vague, impossible metrics.
scenes.caption_roman: Sign two: moving goalposts. Projects you delivered perfectly are suddenly critiqued with vague, impossible metrics.

scenes.caption: Sign three: calendar isolation. Your 1-on-1s get canceled last minute, and your high-impact responsibilities are quietly reassigned.
scenes.caption_roman: Sign three: calendar isolation. Your 1-on-1s get canceled last minute, and your high-impact responsibilities are quietly reassigned.

scenes.caption: Corporate psychologists call this constructive dismissal. They want you to quit so they avoid severance and unemployment payouts.
scenes.caption_roman: Corporate psychologists call this constructive dismissal. They want you to quit so they avoid severance and unemployment payouts.

scenes.caption: Your defense: document every interaction in writing, forward receipts to your personal email, and never resign without consulting employment law. Follow Coercion Files for workplace power dynamics.
